scope: Map the legal successor regime after Law No.708 by separating national/public teachers from private-school teachers, and test whether the temporary Article 13 prohibition simply vanished on repeal.

findings.claim: The 1963 State Public Officials Act independently prohibited public officials from labor movements and other collective activity outside public duties.
findings.evidence: Law No.1325, promulgated 1963-04-17 and effective 1963-06-01, contains Article 66(1): public officials shall not engage in labor movements or other collective acts for matters other than public duties, except officials engaged in de facto labor.
findings.significance: The general public-service restriction existed before Law No.708 was repealed, so repeal cannot be modeled as a return to the 1960 legal position.

findings.claim: National/public teachers were connected to the general public-service duty regime through the Education Public Officials Act.
findings.evidence: The 1963-1964 Education Public Officials Act version identifies national/public school teachers as education public officials; historical Article 43 is titled State Public Officials Act mutatis-mutandis application. Exact incorporated article range should still be transcribed from the official promulgated version/Gazette.

findings.claim: The 1963 Private School Act created a separate successor bridge for private-school teachers rather than making them public officials.
findings.evidence: Private School Act Law No.1362 was enacted 1963-06-26 and effective 1963-07-27. Article 55 provides that rules concerning duties of national/public school teachers apply mutatis mutandis to private-school teachers. This is a service-rule bridge, not conversion of private teachers into public officials.

findings.claim: The successor regime preserved the specific collective class-refusal concept for private-school teachers.
findings.evidence: Private School Act Article 58(1)(4) provides dismissal grounds for political movement, collective refusal of classes, or directing/agitating students for or against a political party. Current consolidated text retains this formulation; secondary legal-history material states the private-teacher service structure dates from the 1963 enactment. The exact 1963 promulgated Article 58 text remains a priority transcription target.
findings.caution: Do not claim exact word-for-word inheritance from Law No.708 Article 13 until the 1963 original Gazette text is pinned.

findings.claim: Law No.708 repeal on 1964-01-01 restored unrestricted teacher labor activity.
findings.evidence: By repeal, State Public Officials Act Article 66 already supplied a general public-official labor/collective-action restriction, while the Private School Act supplied a private-teacher service/dismissal framework. The successor architecture therefore split by employment status instead of disappearing.

findings.claim: The 1961-06-21 Teachers Organization Bill supplied the wording of State Public Officials Act Article 66, Private School Act Articles 55/58, or Law No.708 Article 13.
findings.evidence: The semantic overlap is now broader, but no June 1961 bill original has been obtained. No textual genealogy is asserted.

events.note: 90헌바27 later confirms Article 66 was treated as applicable to education public officials; useful for legal lineage, not evidence of 1961 intent.

adversarial_checks: Repeal of a temporary statute does not imply restoration when overlapping permanent statutes are already effective.
State Public Officials Act Article 66 applies through public-official status; it must not be silently generalized to all private teachers.
Private School Act Article 55 is a mutatis-mutandis service-rule bridge, not a declaration that private teachers are public officials.
Later constitutional cases confirm application history but cannot prove the drafters' 1961 intent.
Semantic similarity between Law 708 Article 13 and State Public Officials Act Article 66 does not establish copying.
Semantic similarity between Law 708 Article 13 and Private School Act collective-class-refusal language does not establish copying without the promulgated 1963 version and drafting file.
The June 1961 Teachers Organization Bill remains a missing ancestor candidate, not a proven ancestor.
Ministerial office does not establish personal authorship of the successor statutes.
A dismissal ground and a criminal prohibition are different legal mechanisms and must remain separate in the event graph.
Public-school and private-school teachers require separate enforcement histories after 1963.
